title: Knowing Your Duty to the World
note: He defines this as knowing the way of the world and acting on it. The books don’t set it out as they do scriptural conduct: you must know it for yourself. After what to avoid in thought, word and deed, this turns to what remains to be done.

couplets.plain: Duty asks for no return. What does the world give back to the rain?
couplets.pm: What do living beings do in return for the clouds that give them water? Nothing. So the duties done by people like those clouds don’t look for a return either. The word for duty itself shows that these things can’t be left undone.

links.reason: Duty done for others looks for nothing in return.

links.quote: What does the world give back to the rain?
What does the world give back to the rain?

couplets.plain: All the wealth you earn by effort is for helping the worthy.
couplets.pm: For the worthy, all the wealth they earn by effort is for doing their duty to others. It isn’t for eating alone, or for hoarding and losing, as with those who help no one.
couplets.note: தக்கார்க்கு can mean “for helping the worthy”, as the plain reading takes it. He takes the worthy as the ones who earn and help.

links.reason: All the wealth earned by effort is said to exist for helping the worthy.

couplets.plain: In the world of the gods or here, it is hard to find anything better than helping others.
couplets.pm: In the world of the gods and in this one, it is hard to find another deed as good as this duty. There, all are alike, with no givers and no takers, so it can’t be done. Here, nothing else suits everyone so well.

links.quote: hard to find anything better than helping others

couplets.plain: Whoever knows what is fitting is alive. Anyone else is counted among the dead.
couplets.pm: The one truly alive is the one who knows the way of the world and acts on it. Anyone who doesn’t, though breathing, is counted one of the dead, since the understanding and action of a living soul aren’t seen in them. A fault in worldly conduct, unlike one in scriptural conduct, has no remedy.
couplets.sensitive: Classes people as good as dead.

links.quote: Whoever knows what is fitting is alive
links.reason: Knowing what is fitting towards others is made the mark of being alive.

couplets.plain: The wealth of a person of great understanding who loves the world is like the village tank filled with water.
couplets.pm: The wealth of someone of great understanding who loves to follow the way of the world is like the tank a village drinks from, filled with water. It doesn’t go to waste, it stands long, and it gives everyone what they need without fail.

links.quote: The wealth of a person of great understanding who loves the world
the village tank filled with water

couplets.plain: When wealth falls to a good person, it is like a fruit tree ripening inside the village.
couplets.pm: When wealth falls to someone who does their duty to others, it is like a useful tree bearing fruit in the middle of the village. Of all worldly justice this duty is the best, so it is the goodness meant here. It gives everyone its use with ease.

links.quote: When wealth falls to a good person
links.reason: A good person’s wealth feeds the people around them.

links.quote: a fruit tree ripening inside the village

couplets.plain: When wealth falls to a person of great worth, it is like a tree that serves as medicine and never fails.
couplets.pm: When wealth falls to someone of great eminence who does this duty, it is like a tree whose every part is medicine for disease and which never fails. Failing means being out of reach, hidden, or out of season. Such a person ignores their own lack and ends everyone’s pain.

links.quote: wealth falls to a person of great worth
links.reason: In the keeping of a person of great worth, wealth goes on relieving need.

links.quote: a tree that serves as medicine and never fails
links.reason: A medicine tree that never fails pictures help that always remains.

couplets.plain: Even when they have little room to give, those who know their duty won’t slacken in helping others.
couplets.pm: Even when their wealth has shrunk, those with the natural understanding that knows what they ought to do won’t weaken in doing this duty. Everything else may go, but not this.

links.quote: those who know their duty won’t slacken in helping others
links.reason: Even lean times do not release those who know their duty.

couplets.plain: A good person’s poverty is this: being unable to rest when they can’t do what they must.
couplets.pm: For someone who does this duty, being poor means the distress of being unable to do the duties they never leave undone. It doesn’t mean going without things to enjoy themselves.

links.quote: A good person’s poverty is this
links.reason: Such a person is poor only on the day they cannot do what they must.

couplets.plain: If helping others brings ruin, that ruin is worth buying, even if you must sell up to do it.
couplets.pm: If anyone says that doing this duty brings loss of wealth, that loss is worth having even by selling yourself. Nothing is worth selling yourself to buy, yet for this you should, because it brings renown. What is lost through this duty is no loss.
couplets.sensitive: says ruining oneself for others is worth it

links.reason: Holds that ruin brought on by helping is worth buying at any price.
